newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Five bidders for Dockland core infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Five bidders for Dockland core infrastructure.

text.p: Five consortiums were shortlisted on Wednesday to develop the trunk infrastructure for the A$2.5 billion Docklands redevelopment on Melbourne's waterfront.
The Docklands Authority announced the consortia were:
- Docklands Infrastructure Consortium, comprising Leighton Contractors, Macquarie Equity Finance, Energy Australia, Optus Networks and Gutteridge Haskins and Davey;
- Docklands Urban Services, comprising Lend Lease Infrastructure, Texas Utilities, Integrated Systems Solutions Corp Australia in association with Australian Water Services;
- Harbourside Infrastructure Consortium, comprising AbiGroup, Telstra Applied Technologies, CitiPower, Barclay Mowlem and Maunsell Pty Ltd;
- Thiess Eastern Energy, comprising Thiess Contractors, Eastern Energy, Ove Arup and Partners, Kinhill Engineers;
- Transervice, comprising Transfield Construction (Victoria), ANZ Global Structured Finance, Sinclair Knight Merz and Powercore Australia Ltd.
The trunk infrastructure includes transport and pedestrian links as well as supply of water, electricity, sewerage and telecommunications.
The authority estimates this infrastructure will cost about A$150 million to build, with the bills being paid by the successful bidders to develop the project site's five precincts.
A separate short-list of 15 bidders has already been drawn up for development of the five precincts.
